profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the research program manager and the quantitative analytics lead at an economic research consultancy preparing a client-facing cross-country briefing on the effects of European Central Bank unconventional policies on stock market volatility using the MAP model framework. The team has parallel workstreams: the analytics side is finalizing forecasts, policy-shock simulations, and country comparisons for four Eurozone markets, while the program side is assembling the briefing deck, executive summary, and data appendix for a bank strategy client. The meeting context is a midweek handoff check after the latest model run. The agenda is to align on what will be delivered for the 'Friday package,' confirm which model outputs are considered final, clarify how the implementation-effect results will feed into slides and appendix materials, and coordinate ownership of the shared results workbook. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on handoffs, file readiness, and what will be included in the client package, even though several second-order assumptions remain misaligned.

members.name: Elena Rossi
members.expertise: Client deliverables, cross-workstream coordination, executive-level reporting, publication packaging
members.background: Elena manages external research deliverables for a macro-financial advisory firm and previously worked in investor communications, where she standardized briefing decks and appendices for institutional clients.
members.private_state: She wants a smooth Friday handoff with no last-minute formatting churn, and is especially concerned about having a polished deck and appendix that can survive compliance review without needing another analytics pass.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'Friday package,' it means the complete client-ready set of materials uploaded by end of business Central European Time on Friday, including deck, appendix, and locked charts.
A result is 'final' once the numbers for the preferred specification are stable enough to place into slides, even if notes and robustness tabs are still being cleaned up.
The 'results workbook' refers to the presentation-linked Excel file in the shared client folder, which is the authoritative source for figures used downstream.
The implementation-effect section naturally includes the country comparison visuals and one concise interpretation note, but not the full simulation mechanics unless someone explicitly asks.
If analytics says the latest run uses the post-EAPP window, that corresponds to the version already referenced in Monday's draft slide titles.

members.name: Matteo Klein
members.expertise: Financial econometrics, volatility modeling, MEM/MAP estimation, forecast evaluation and simulation
members.background: Matteo leads the quantitative workstream for macro-market studies and previously worked in an academic econometrics lab, where reproducibility, versioned code, and technical appendices were the default standard.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid the client seeing partially documented results, and is focused on making sure the MAP outputs, policy-shock scenarios, and model-confidence-set tables are internally reproducible before they are treated as frozen.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'Friday package,' it means the analytics handoff bundle sent by Friday evening, consisting of validated outputs, code-linked tables, and technical notes that the program team can still package afterward.
A result is 'final' only when the estimation run, forecast tables, chart exports, and methodological notes all reconcile in the version-controlled analytics directory.
The 'results workbook' refers to the master analysis workbook generated from the latest scripts in the research drive, not the client-facing Excel file assembled for slides.

The implementation-effect section includes the full set of horizon-by-horizon forecast effects and policy-shock assumptions because those are needed to interpret the volatility reduction claim correctly.
The post-EAPP run means the latest specification using the revised event coding from Tuesday night, which supersedes any outputs circulated earlier in the week.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to have the Friday package ready
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the full client-ready deliverable set must be complete in the client folder by Friday end of business CET, including polished slides, appendix, and finalized linked figures.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Matteo means the analytics handoff materials will be ready by Friday evening for internal transfer, after which packaging into client-ready form can continue.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination settings, 'Friday package' sounds like a settled shared milestone, and both participants reasonably assume the other is using the team's familiar shorthand rather than needing a boundary clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to using the final results for the briefing
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena treats results as final once the headline numbers and charts for the preferred model are stable enough to place into slides without expecting substantive directional changes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Matteo treats results as final only after documentation, table reconciliation, and reproducibility checks are complete for the latest versioned run.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use a common professional term associated with normal workflow maturity, but each applies a different threshold that is routine in their own function and therefore too obvious to spell out.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both mention updating the results workbook
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is referring to the client-shareable Excel workbook in the shared delivery folder that feeds the deck links and appendix tables.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Matteo is referring to the master analysis workbook in the research drive generated from the latest MAP scripts and tied to version-controlled outputs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There is already a workbook with the same informal name in each workstream, and because both are used regularly in handoffs, the phrase sounds unambiguous inside the meeting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to include the implementation-effect section
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena expects a concise section made of country comparison charts, one short interpretation paragraph, and a simple appendix note sufficient for an executive client briefing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Matteo expects to deliver a technically complete section containing horizon-by-horizon effects, policy-shock setup details, and methodological notes so the interpretation is properly qualified.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They agree on the same content label and overall purpose, but each silently imports the standard production method from their role—executive packaging versus technical research documentation.

I mainly need a clean handoff so production and compliance don't get dragged into late churn.
